An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ and $E$ be the oriented boundaries of the standard one-boundary square plumbings of two positive Hopf bands and of one positive with one negative Hopf band, respectively; these are the right-handed trefoil and the figure-eight knot. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose induced boundary components have linking number $+1$; its core, the central simple closed curve, has self-pairing $-1$. a negative Hopf band has boundary linking number $-1$ and core self-pairing $+1$. A square plumbing identifies a square in the boundary collars of the two annuli so that its edges alternate between them, then smooths the corners; use the gluing for which the resulting boundary is one component. Order the two cores $a,b$ with the positive Hopf core first, orient them so $a\cdot_F b=+1$, and use the standard plumbing side for which $a^+$ bounds a disk disjoint from $b$. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$, their Seifert matrices are

$$V_T=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V_E=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Their determinant representatives are $\Delta_T(t)=1-t+t^2$ and $\Delta_E(t)=-1+3t-t^2$. They both evaluate to $1$ at $t=1$; at $t=-1$ the displayed representatives evaluate to $3$ and $-5$, so the unit-invariant absolute values are $3$ and $5$. These determinant classes are unchanged up to units by oriented ambient isotopy and integral basis changes. The connected sum satisfies

$$\Delta_{T\#E}(t)\doteq(1-t+t^2)(-1+3t-t^2)=-t^4+4t^3-5t^2+4t-1.$$

This displayed representative has values $1$ at $t=1$ and $-15$ at $t=-1$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its boundary orientation is the given orientation of $K$. Let $g$ be the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of the first singular homology group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, represented by integral one-cycles on $F$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. The positive push-off $a_i^+$ is the cycle carried to a sufficiently small positive normal level in a bicollar of $F$.

For disjoint oriented closed curves $J,L\subset S^3$, orient a meridian $\mu_L$ of $L$ so that a positive tangent to $L$ followed by a positive basis of its normal disk gives the ambient orientation. The linking number $\operatorname{lk}(J,L)$ is the integer determined by $[J]=\operatorname{lk}(J,L)[\mu_L]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$, using the Alexander-duality identification that sends $[\mu_L]$ to $1$. Extend linking additively over integral one-cycles. The Seifert pairing is $\theta_F(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$, and its matrix in the chosen basis is $V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{2g}$, where $V_{ij}=\theta_F(a_i,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The surface and basis are part of the data; this definition asserts no knot-only matrix invariant.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be any ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $J_F$ be the matrix of the algebraic intersection form on $F$, with a transverse intersection of oriented curves $u,v$ counted positively exactly when their ordered tangent vectors form a positive basis of $TF$. Then $V-V^T=J_F$. The matrix $J_F$ is skew-symmetric and unimodular; when $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ is a standard handle basis, it is a direct sum of blocks $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$.

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot and $F$ a connected compact smooth oriented spanning surface of genus $g$. The Seifert matrix $V$ defines a function on $H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)$ by
$$q_F([x])=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,x)\pmod2=x^TVx\pmod2,$$
where an integral lift of the mod-two homology class is used in the last expression. Its polarization is the mod-two intersection form. A symplectic basis is an ordered basis $(a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_g,b_g)$ with $a_i\cdot b_j=\delta_{ij}$ and all other pairings zero. Define
$$\operatorname{Arf}(q_F)=\sum_{i=1}^g q_F(a_i)q_F(b_i)\pmod2.$$
The quadratic-enhancement lemma proves that this value is independent of symplectic basis; the S-equivalence and Conway bridge proves independence of $F$, so the resulting knot invariant is denoted $\operatorname{Arf}(K)$. For $g=0$ the empty sum is $0$.

Assume full AC and let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. With the normalized Conway polynomial $\nabla_K(z)=1+a_2(K)z^2+a_4(K)z^4+\cdots$ and the Seifert-form definition of $\operatorname{Arf}(K)$,
$$\operatorname{Arf}(K)=a_2(K)\pmod2.$$

Assume full AC. For every $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$, changing an ordered basis by an integral unimodular congruence or changing a knot Seifert matrix by either elementary enlargement or reduction preserves the signature of $H_\omega$. Consequently, the nonroot Levine–Tristram signature and its one-sided-average value at every Alexander root are independent of the spanning surface and basis.

derivations.claim: Since $1-(-1)=2$, $H_{-1}(V)=2(V+V^T)$. For the trefoil, $V_T+V_T^T=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1\\-1&-2\end{pmatrix}$ has eigenvalues $-1,-3$, so the signature is $-2$. For the figure-eight, $V_F+V_F^T=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$ has determinant $-5<0$, hence one positive and one negative eigenvalue, so the signature is $0$.

The standard intersection block is $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$ for both matrices. The quadratic values on the basis vectors are their diagonal entries modulo two, namely $(1,1)$ for each matrix. Therefore $\operatorname{Arf}=1\cdot1=1$ for each knot. Their Alexander determinants are $\det(V_T-tV_T^T)=1-t+t^2$ and $\det(V_F-tV_F^T)=-1+3t-t^2$. Substituting $t^{1/2}-t^{-1/2}=z$ with the symmetric normalization gives $\nabla_T=1+z^2$ and $\nabla_F=1-z^2$; both $z^2$ coefficients are odd, agreeing with the Arf values.
